I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether lying to my boyfriend about seeing his ex-girlfriend at a party is right or wrong. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We've been dating for four months, and he was previously dating another girl for two years. They broke up because he suspected she was cheating based on rumors about a party where she supposedly danced and kissed another guy. I was also at that party, but I don't remember seeing her because it was a huge event with a lot of people, and we didn't have overlapping friend circles. When we started dating, he was still really hurt about the breakup and was questioning whether they should have stayed together. It was really painful to see him like that, and all I wanted was for us to have a fresh start. I didn't want him to be stuck in the past, so when he asked me if I had seen his ex at the party, I lied and said I had seen her with other guys. This seemed to help him move on faster, and he's much happier now. He says he feels better knowing that she definitely cheated, and he has no regrets about the breakup. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by lying and keeping up the lie. On one hand, I wanted to help him feel better and move on from the past. On the other hand, lying feels wrong, and I'm worried about the long-term consequences of this lie. Could it affect our trust in each other? What if he finds out the truth someday? Is it better to tell the truth now, even if it might upset him again? I also need to consider why I lied in the first place. Was it to protect him from further pain, or was it to protect myself from feeling guilty or responsible for his hurt? Understanding my own motivations might help me decide whether the lie was justified or not. Another thing to think about is the impact of the lie on our relationship. Trust is a fundamental aspect of any relationship, and lying can erode that trust. Even if the lie was intended to help, it might still have negative consequences. I should also consider how he would feel if he found out I lied, and whether that would be more hurtful than the truth. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Could I have told him the truth in a way that still acknowledged his feelings and helped him move on without lying? Maybe by being honest about not seeing her but still validating his feelings about the breakup. Overall, I'm torn between wanting to protect him and wanting to maintain honesty in our relationship. I need to weigh the immediate benefits of the lie against the potential long-term damage it could cause. It's a tough situation, and I'm not sure what the right decision is.
